Apple has surged 28% this year to record highs, powered by solid early demand for the newly launched iPhone Duo despite tight supply.

Apple's rally dwarfs Microsoft's 9% and Alphabet's 3% gains, while its top weighting in XLK and SPY quietly amplifies Apple exposure for index fund investors.

Are you ahead, or behind on retirement? SmartAsset's free tool can match you with a financial advisor in minutes to help you answer that today. Each advisor has been carefully vetted, and must act in your best interests. Don't waste another minute; learn more here.

A year of steady gains has put Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) in step with the entire technology sector and well ahead of its biggest mega-cap rivals. That turns the choice between banking profits and holding on into a live debate. Apple stock is down 0.6% to $346.32 in afternoon trading, a shallow dip that leaves its gain this year at 28%.

Vytautas Kielaitis/Shutterstock.com

The Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSEARCA:XLK) is up 28% this year, matching Apple stock. For a broad-market gauge, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 12% this year. That leaves Apple stock and the XLK technology fund far in front of the broad market.

Meanwhile, Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) stock is up 9% this year to $524.26, a gain that trails Apple stock by a wide margin. Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) stock is up 3% this year to $322.16, the smallest advance among these particular tech stocks. That gap frames the central question for Apple shareholders: whether a record-setting run still has room to extend.

AAPL Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
iPhone Duo Demand Powers Apple's Record Run

Apple's newest product is driving the company's momentum. The iPhone Duo began its first weeks on sale this month, the same stretch in which Apple stock reached record highs. Analysts have described early demand as solid, a meaningful signal for a company that earns most of its revenue from iPhone sales.

Broyhill Asset Management, a Charlotte-based firm, issued its third-quarter 2026 investor letter. The letter can be downloaded here. The Broyhill Equity Composite decreased by 0.3% in Q3, underperforming the MSCI All Country World Index, which gained 1.7%. For the first nine months of the year, the Composite returned 1.9%, compared to 13.4% for the Index. The quarter was characterized by a strong July, when the Composite rose by 3.3%, despite a significant fall in the semiconductor index. However, technology stocks led in August and September, while other sectors, including consumer staples and industrials, declined, leading to the decline. Broyhill cites rising oil prices, higher interest rates, and competition for capital as reasons to be cautious. The recent performance of Broyhill has been analyzed due to its divergence from the overall market trend. Despite this, the firm is confident in its portfolio's ability to adapt to varying economic conditions. Broyhill is committed to focusing on fundamental drivers and valuations while exploring new opportunities, valuing the trust of its investors and its long-term partners. Also, check the Fund's top five holdings to see its best picks for 2026.

In its Q3 2026 investor letter, Broyhill Asset Management highlighted Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) as a top contributor. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) is a multinational software company that develops and supports software, services, devices, and solutions, holding dominant positions in software, cloud infrastructure, generative AI, and gaming. On October 23, 2026, Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) closed at $521.08 per share, reflecting a market capitalization of $3.87 trillion. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) posted a one‑month return of 0.95%, while its shares declined 0.48% over the past 52 weeks.

Broyhill Asset Management stated the following regarding Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

"Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) added about 110 basis points, most of it in July, the month we added to the position. Results for its fiscal fourth quarter were ahead of expectations, led by faster growth in Azure, its cloud platform, with guidance for further acceleration. Demand continues to exceed capacity, and adoption of its Copilot AI assistant keeps widening. What mattered most for this quarter's theme was cash: capital spending came in below expectations, free cash flow was strong, and management expects to be free cash flow positive next year at a time when the market worried about hyperscalers competing for capital. The shares rose 16% the next day."

Adobe is down 26.75% year to date and sits well below its 52-week high of $363.70, though it has climbed off the $190.12 low. Momentum has turned recently, with shares up 8.51% over the past week and 3% over the past month.

In fiscal Q3, revenue came in at $6.76 billion, up 12.9% and ahead of the $6.70 billion consensus. Non-GAAP EPS of $6.13 topped the $6.09 estimate, making it the fifth beat in a row.

Investment management company Vulcan Value Partners recently released its third-quarter 2026 investor letter. The letter can be downloaded here. The portfolio reported a strong quarter, with all strategies except Small Cap reporting positive absolute results, with Small Cap down about 1%. In the quarter, the Large Cap Composite (Net) returned 7.4%, the Small Cap Composite (Net) returned -1.2%, the Focus Composite (Net) returned 8.9%, the Focus Plus Composite (Net) returned 8.8%, and the All-Cap Composite (Net) returned 7.5%. The firm emphasized its focus on long-term intrinsic value, noting that portfolio price-to-value ratios remain historically low and that it believes this is an attractive time to invest. The firm remains optimistic about its holdings' long-term value growth, competitive advantages, and ability to compound cash flows. Also, check the Fund's top five holdings to see its best picks for 2026.

In its Q3 2026 investor letter, Vulcan Value Partners highlighted Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) as a top contributor. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) is a multinational software company that develops and supports software, services, devices, and solutions, holding dominant positions in software, cloud infrastructure, generative AI, and gaming. On October 22, 2026, Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) closed at $521.08 per share, reflecting a market capitalization of $3.87 trillion. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) posted a one‑month return of 0.95%, while its shares declined 0.48% over the past 52 weeks.

Vulcan Value Partners stated the following regarding Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

"Going into the quarter, Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) was one of our most discounted names and also one of our highest quality businesses. The stock was up after reporting fiscal fourth quarter results. Most notably, Azure growth accelerated to 43%, its highest growth rate in four years. Management noted that demand for Azure services continues to exceed supply, and annual Azure revenue now exceeds $100 billion. Microsoft's commercial remaining performance obligation grew 84% year-over-year, or 25% excluding its contracts with OpenAI. Also, after an initial lukewarm response to Microsoft's Copilot, paid Copilot subscribers now exceed 30 million, demonstrating broad enterprise adoption. Microsoft also introduced autonomous agent features within Copilot that make the product more useful and stickier for its users. Lastly, while free cash flow is down as Microsoft invests in additional compute capacity, it was still quite substantial. Microsoft generated $20 billion in free cash flow in fiscal fourth quarter and $67 billion in fiscal year 2026. Microsoft's value has grown meaningfully, its competitive advantages are intact, and shares remain significantly discounted."
